risks: Low: all students receive eight sessions of examination-skills teaching; the risk is a small difference in examination preparation between arms.
consent: Students are told about the evaluation at the start of the year and may ask for their data to be excluded; allocation follows the normal timetable process.
data: Assessment and attendance data are de-identified by the assessment office before analysis under approval ERC-2026-14.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: students with caring duties, paid work, disabilities or who study in a second language may be affected differently. Sessions are timetabled within the normal day, learning adjustments continue in both arms, and pass rates are reported by arm for groups large enough to protect anonymity.
effectiveness: The school keeps the change only if pass rates are maintained with stated uncertainty.
efficiency: Near-peer teaching may release faculty time for clinical teaching elsewhere.
costs: Staff time within existing roles; tutor payments already budgeted.
grants: A small education research grant could fund the 2028 extension.
partnerships: Assessment office, finance office, student representatives and the near-peer tutor society.
rebPath: Approved by the education research committee on 2026-09-17 (ERC-2026-14) as evaluation of routine teaching with de-identified data, under TCPS 2 guidance for education research.
limitations: One school and one year; allocation by timetable is not randomisation.
summary: Low-risk education evaluation with de-identified data, an opt-out and equity reporting.
